discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can turn an ordinary band insulator into a new state of matter, the quantum spin Hall insulator, classified by a Z2 topological invariant and protected by time-reversal symmetry, with helical edge states immune to backscattering. Their work generalized the topology of the quantum Hall effect to systems without magnetic fields and, with its three-dimensional extension, created the field of topological insulators. Molenkamp's 2007 observation of quantized edge conductance in HgTe quantum wells provided the decisive experimental realization, followed by nonlocal transport proof of helical edge channels. This is a model case of theory and experiment advancing together: a simple, transparent band-structure idea making a sharp prediction, confirmed in engineered materials. Topological band theory now pervades condensed-matter physics, underpinning the quantum anomalous Hall effect, Weyl semimetals, topological superconductivity and topological photonics.
